sanskrit: hanyamāne bale tūrṇam anyonyaṃ te mahāmṛdhe sarasīva mahāgharme sūpakṣīṇe babhūvatuḥ
english: As their armies were swiftly slaughtering each other in that great battle, those two forces became like a pond in the height of summer, greatly diminished on both sides.

sanskrit: svabalasya vighātena virūpākṣavadhena ca babhūva dviguṇaṃ kruddho rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: At the destruction of his own army and at the slaying of Virūpākṣa, Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, became doubly enraged.

sanskrit: prakṣīṇaṃ tu balaṃ dṛṣṭvā vadhyamānaṃ valīmukhaiḥ babhūvāsya vyathā yuddhe prekṣya daivaviparyayam
english: Seeing his army decimated, being slaughtered by the vānaras, anguish arose in him in the battle as he beheld the reversal of fortune brought by destiny.

sanskrit: uvāca ca samīpasthaṃ mahodaram ariṃdamam asmin kāle mahābāho jayāśā tvayi me sthitā
english: He then spoke to Mahodara, the subduer of foes, who stood nearby: "At this moment, O mighty-armed one, my hope of victory rests in you."

sanskrit: jahi śatrucamūṃ vīra darśayādya parākramam bhartṛpiṇḍasya kālo 'yaṃ nirveṣṭuṃ sādhu yudhyatām
english: "Destroy the enemy's army, O hero; show your valor today. This is the time to repay the master's bread — fight well!"

sanskrit: evam uktas tathety uktvā rākṣasendraṃ mahodaraḥ praviveśārisenāṃ sa pataṃga iva pāvakam
english: Thus addressed, Mahodara said "So be it" to the lord of rākṣasas, and plunged into the enemy's army like a moth into fire.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa kadanaṃ cakre vānarāṇāṃ mahābalaḥ bhartṛvākyena tejasvī svena vīryeṇa coditaḥ
english: Then that mighty, brilliant one wrought devastation among the vānaras, driven on by his master's words and by his own valor.

sanskrit: prabhagnāṃ samare dṛṣṭvā vānarāṇāṃ mahācamūm abhidudrāva sugrīvo mahodaram anantaram
english: Seeing the great army of the vānaras being broken in battle, Sugrīva immediately charged at Mahodara.

sanskrit: pragṛhya vipulāṃ ghorāṃ mahīdharasamāṃ śilām cikṣepa ca mahātejās tad vadhāya harīśvaraḥ
english: Seizing a vast, terrible boulder equal to a mountain, the lord of monkeys, blazing with great energy, hurled it for his destruction.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā śilāṃ dṛṣṭvā mahodaraḥ asaṃbhrāntas tato bāṇair nirbibheda durāsadām
english: Seeing that boulder rushing upon him, Mahodara, unperturbed, shattered it with arrows — that thing so difficult to withstand.

sanskrit: rakṣasā tena bāṇaughair nikṛttā sā sahasradhā nipapāta śilā bhūmau gṛdhracakram ivākulam
english: Cut to pieces by that rākṣasa with volleys of arrows, the boulder fell to the ground in a thousand fragments, like a swirling cluster of vultures scattered in confusion.

sanskrit: tāṃ tu bhinnāṃ śilāṃ dṛṣṭvā sugrīvaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ sālam utpāṭya cikṣepa rakṣase raṇamūrdhani śaraiś ca vidadārainaṃ śūraḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: Seeing that boulder shattered, Sugrīva, overcome with rage, uprooted a sāla tree and hurled it at the rākṣasa in the forefront of battle, and that hero, conqueror of enemy cities, also tore into him with arrows.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa tataḥ kruddhaḥ parighaṃ patitaṃ bhuvi āvidhya tu sa taṃ dīptaṃ parighaṃ tasya darśayan parighāgreṇa vegena jaghānāsya hayottamān
english: Then in his rage he spotted an iron club lying on the ground; whirling that blazing iron club and displaying it, he swiftly struck Sugrīva's finest horses with its tip.

sanskrit: tasmād dhatahayād vīraḥ so 'vaplutya mahārathāt gadāṃ jagrāha saṃkruddho rākṣaso 'tha mahodaraḥ
english: The heroic rākṣasa Mahodara, intensely enraged, leaped down from that great chariot whose horses had been slain, and seized his mace.

sanskrit: gadāparighahastau tau yudhi vīrau samīyatuḥ nardantau govṛṣaprakhyau ghanāv iva savidyutau
english: Those two warriors, each with mace and iron club in hand, came together in battle, roaring like bull-elephants, like two storm-clouds accompanied by lightning.

sanskrit: ājaghāna gadāṃ tasya parigheṇa harīśvaraḥ papāta sa gadodbhinnaḥ parighas tasya bhūtale
english: The lord of monkeys struck Mahodara's mace with his iron club; split apart by the mace, that club of his fell to the ground.

sanskrit: tato jagrāha tejasvī sugrīvo vasudhātalāt āyasaṃ musalaṃ ghoraṃ sarvato hemabhūṣitam
english: Then the radiant Sugrīva picked up from the ground a terrible iron pestle adorned all over with gold.

sanskrit: taṃ samudyamya cikṣepa so 'py anyāṃ vyākṣipad gadām bhinnāv anyonyam āsādya petatur dharaṇītale
english: Raising it, he threw it; Mahodara likewise hurled another mace at him. Striking each other, both shattered and fell to the ground.

sanskrit: tato bhagnapraharaṇau muṣṭibhyāṃ tau samīyatuḥ tejobalasamāviṣṭau dīptāv iva hutāśanau
english: Then, with their weapons broken, those two came together with bare fists, both possessed of equal blazing energy, like two flaming fires.

sanskrit: jaghnatus tau tadānyonyaṃ nedatuś ca punaḥ punaḥ talaiś cānyonyam āhatya petatur dharaṇītale
english: Those two struck each other and roared again and again; striking each other with their palms, they fell to the ground.

sanskrit: utpetatus tatas tūrṇaṃ jaghnatuś ca parasparam bhujaiś cikṣepatur vīrāv anyonyam aparājitau
english: They quickly sprang up again and struck each other; those two unconquered warriors threw each other with their arms.

sanskrit: ājahāra tadā khaḍgam adūraparivartinam rākṣasaś carmaṇā sārdhaṃ mahāvego mahodaraḥ
english: Then the swift Mahodara, the rākṣasa, seized a sword that lay near at hand, together with a shield.

sanskrit: tathaiva ca mahākhaḍgaṃ carmaṇā patitaṃ saha jagrāha vānaraśreṣṭhaḥ sugrīvo vegavattaraḥ
english: Similarly, the foremost of vānaras, Sugrīva, even swifter, seized a great sword along with its fallen shield.

sanskrit: tau tu roṣaparītāṅgau nardantāv abhyadhāvatām udyatāsī raṇe hṛṣṭau yudhi śastraviśāradau
english: Those two, their bodies overcome with fury, roaring, charged at each other with swords raised in battle, both exhilarated and expert in weaponry in combat.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇaṃ maṇḍalaṃ cobhau tau tūrṇaṃ saṃparīyatuḥ anyonyam abhisaṃkruddhau jaye praṇihitāv ubhau
english: Both swiftly circled the right-hand arc; both were intensely enraged at each other, both intent on victory.

sanskrit: sa tu śūro mahāvego vīryaślāghī mahodaraḥ mahācarmaṇi taṃ khaḍgaṃ pātayām āsa durmatiḥ
english: That hero, the swift Mahodara, boastful of his valor but wicked-minded, brought his sword down upon Sugrīva's great shield.

sanskrit: lagnam utkarṣataḥ khaḍgaṃ khaḍgena kapikuñjaraḥ jahāra saśiras trāṇaṃ kuṇḍalopahitaṃ śiraḥ
english: As Mahodara was pulling free his sword embedded in the shield, the foremost among monkeys severed his head along with its protective helmet adorned with earrings.

sanskrit: nikṛttaśirasas tasya patitasya mahītale tad balaṃ rākṣasendrasya dṛṣṭvā tatra na tiṣṭhati
english: Seeing him fall to the ground with his head severed, the army of the lord of rākṣasas did not remain there.

sanskrit: hatvā taṃ vānaraiḥ sārdhaṃ nanāda mudito hariḥ cukrodha ca daśagrīvo babhau hṛṣṭaś ca rāghavaḥ
english: Having slain him, that monkey roared joyfully together with the other vānaras; the ten-headed Rāvaṇa was furious, while Rāghava shone with delight.

sanskrit: mahodare tu nihate mahāpārśvo mahābalaḥ aṅgadasya camūṃ bhīmāṃ kṣobhayām āsa sāyakaiḥ
english: When Mahodara had been slain, the mighty Mahāpārśva began to harass Aṅgada's formidable army with his arrows.

sanskrit: sa vānarāṇāṃ mukhyānām uttamāṅgāni sarvaśaḥ pātayām āsa kāyebhyaḥ phalaṃ vṛntād ivānilaḥ
english: He caused the heads of the foremost among the vānaras to fall from their bodies on all sides, as the wind knocks fruit from its stalk.

sanskrit: keṣāṃ cid iṣubhir bāhūn skandhāṃś cicheda rākṣasaḥ vānarāṇāṃ susaṃkruddhaḥ pārśvaṃ keṣāṃ vyadārayat
english: That rākṣasa, greatly enraged, cut off the arms and shoulders of some vānaras with his arrows, and tore open the flanks of others.

sanskrit: te 'rditā bāṇavarṣeṇa mahāpārśvena vānarāḥ viṣādavimukhāḥ sarve babhūvur gatacetasaḥ
english: Those vānaras, tormented by the shower of arrows from Mahāpārśva, all turned away in despair, their senses gone.

sanskrit: nirīkṣya balam udvignam aṅgado rākṣasārditam vegaṃ cakre mahābāhuḥ samudra iva parvaṇi
english: Observing his army distressed and afflicted by the rākṣasa, mighty-armed Aṅgada surged forward like the ocean at the full moon.

sanskrit: āyasaṃ parighaṃ gṛhya sūryaraśmisamaprabham samare vānaraśreṣṭho mahāpārśve nyapātayat
english: Seizing an iron club equal in brilliance to the rays of the sun, the foremost of vānaras brought it down upon Mahāpārśva in battle.

sanskrit: sa tu tena prahāreṇa mahāpārśvo vicetanaḥ sasūtaḥ syandanāt tasmād visaṃjñaḥ prāpatad bhuvi
english: By that blow, Mahāpārśva was rendered unconscious; together with his charioteer, senseless, he fell from his chariot to the ground.

sanskrit: sarkṣarājas tu tejasvī nīlāñjanacayopamaḥ niṣpatya sumahāvīryaḥ svād yūthān meghasaṃnibhāt
english: Then the splendid lord of the bears, resembling a heap of blue collyrium, of surpassing valor, leaped forth from his own troop that was like a thunder-cloud.

sanskrit: pragṛhya giriśṛṅgābhāṃ kruddhaḥ sa vipulāṃ śilām aśvāñ jaghāna tarasā syandanaṃ ca babhañja tam
english: Seizing a huge boulder resembling a mountain-peak, he in his fury swiftly struck the horses down and smashed that chariot to pieces.

sanskrit: muhūrtāl labdhasaṃjñas tu mahāpārśvo mahābalaḥ aṅgadaṃ bahubhir bāṇair bhūyas taṃ pratyavidhyata
english: But after a moment, mighty Mahāpārśva regained consciousness and pierced Aṅgada again with many arrows.

sanskrit: jāmbavantaṃ tribhir bāṇair ājaghāna stanāntare ṛkṣarājaṃ gavākṣaṃ ca jaghāna bahubhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: He struck Jāmbavān with three arrows in the middle of his chest, and struck the king of the bears, Gavākṣa, with many arrows.

sanskrit: gavākṣaṃ jāmbavantaṃ ca sa dṛṣṭvā śarapīḍitau jagrāha parighaṃ ghoram aṅgadaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ
english: Seeing Gavākṣa and Jāmbavān tormented by arrows, Aṅgada, overcome with rage, seized his terrible iron club.

sanskrit: tasyāṅgadaḥ prakupito rākṣasasya tam āyasaṃ dūrasthitasya parighaṃ raviraśmisamaprabham
english: Aṅgada, greatly enraged at that rākṣasa who stood at a distance, seized that iron club of his, equal in radiance to the rays of the sun,

sanskrit: dvābhyāṃ bhujābhyāṃ saṃgṛhya bhrāmayitvā ca vegavān mahāpārśvāya cikṣepa vadhārthaṃ vālinaḥ sutaḥ
english: grasping it with both arms, and whirling it, the swift son of Vālin hurled it at Mahāpārśva for his destruction.

sanskrit: sa tu kṣipto balavatā parighas tasya rakṣasaḥ dhanuś ca saśaraṃ hastāc chirastraṃ cāpy apātayat
english: That club hurled by the powerful one knocked the rākṣasa's bow together with its arrow from his hand, and also struck off his helmet.

sanskrit: taṃ samāsādya vegena vāliputraḥ pratāpavān talenābhyahanat kruddhaḥ karṇamūle sakuṇḍale
english: Swiftly closing in, the powerful son of Vālin, in his rage, struck him with his open palm at the root of the ear adorned with its earring.

sanskrit: sa tu kruddho mahāvego mahāpārśvo mahādyutiḥ kareṇaikena jagrāha sumahāntaṃ paraśvadham
english: Enraged, the swift Mahāpārśva of great splendor seized in one hand a very large battle-axe.

sanskrit: taṃ tailadhautaṃ vimalaṃ śailasāramayaṃ dṛḍham rākṣasaḥ paramakruddho vāliputre nyapātayat
english: That axe — burnished with oil, gleaming, made of the finest stone, hard — the rākṣasa, extremely furious, brought down upon the son of Vālin.

sanskrit: tena vāmāṃsaphalake bhṛśaṃ pratyavapātitam aṅgado mokṣayām āsa saroṣaḥ sa paraśvadham
english: When it landed violently on his left shoulder-blade, Aṅgada, enraged, wrenched the battle-axe free.

sanskrit: sa vīro vajrasaṃkāśam aṅgado muṣṭim ātmanaḥ saṃvartayan susaṃkruddhaḥ pitus tulyaparākramaḥ
english: That hero Aṅgada, equal in valor to his father, intensely enraged, drew back his fist resembling a thunderbolt,

sanskrit: rākṣasasya stanābhyāśe marmajño hṛdayaṃ prati indrāśanisamasparśaṃ sa muṣṭiṃ vinyapātayat
english: and, knowing the vital points, he brought down that fist — equal in impact to Indra's thunderbolt — squarely upon the rākṣasa's chest, aimed at the heart.

sanskrit: tena tasya nipātena rākṣasasya mahāmṛdhe paphāla hṛdayaṃ cāśu sa papāta hato bhuvi
english: By that blow in that great battle, the rākṣasa's heart instantly burst, and he fell slain to the ground.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite bhūmau tat sainyaṃ saṃpracukṣubhe abhavac ca mahān krodhaḥ samare rāvaṇasya tu
english: When he fell to the ground, that army was thrown into turmoil, and great rage arose in Rāvaṇa during the battle.

sanskrit: mahodaramahāpārśvau hatau dṛṣṭvā tu rākṣasau tasmiṃś ca nihate vīre virūpākṣe mahābale
english: Seeing the two rākṣasas Mahodara and Mahāpārśva slain, and the mighty warrior Virūpākṣa also killed,

sanskrit: āviveśa mahān krodho rāvaṇaṃ tu mahāmṛdhe sūtaṃ saṃcodayām āsa vākyaṃ cedam uvāca ha
english: great rage entered Rāvaṇa in that mighty battle. He urged on his charioteer and spoke these words:

sanskrit: nihatānām amātyānāṃ ruddhasya nagarasya ca duḥkham eṣo 'paneṣyāmi hatvā tau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: "I shall remove this grief of mine for my slain ministers and my besieged city by killing both Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: rāmavṛkṣaṃ raṇe hanmi sītāpuṣpaphalapradam praśākhā yasya sugrīvo jāmbavān kumudo nalaḥ
english: "I shall fell the tree that is Rāma in battle — that tree bearing Sītā as its flower and fruit, whose branches are Sugrīva, Jāmbavān, Kumuda, and Nala."

sanskrit: sa diśo daśa ghoṣeṇa rathasyātiratho mahān nādayan prayayau tūrṇaṃ rāghavaṃ cābhyavartata
english: That supreme chariot-warrior, that great one, making all ten directions resound with the thunder of his chariot, swiftly proceeded and charged toward Rāghava.

sanskrit: pūritā tena śabdena sanadīgirikānanā saṃcacāla mahī sarvā savarāhamṛgadvipā
english: The earth entire, with its rivers, mountains and forests, filled with that sound, shook — together with its boars, deer, and elephants.

sanskrit: tāmasaṃ sumahāghoraṃ cakārāstraṃ sudāruṇam nirdadāha kapīn sarvāṃs te prapetuḥ samantataḥ
english: He unleashed the dark weapon, immensely terrible and most dreadful, which consumed all the monkeys utterly; they fled in every direction.

sanskrit: tāny anīkāny anekāni rāvaṇasya śarottamaiḥ dṛṣṭvā bhagnāni śataśas tatra rāghavaḥ paryavasthitaḥ
english: Seeing those many armies broken into hundreds of fragments by Rāvaṇa's excellent arrows, Rāghava stood firm there.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa tataḥ rāmaṃ tiṣṭhantam aparājitam lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā viṣṇunā vāsavaṃ yathā
english: He then saw Rāma standing unconquered together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa, as Viṣṇu stands with Vāsava.

sanskrit: ālikhantam ivākāśaṃ avaṣṭabhya mahad dhanuḥ padmapatraviśālākṣaṃ dīrghabāhum ariṃdamam
english: Rāma seemed to be drawing lines in the sky as he grasped his great bow — broad-eyed as lotus petals, long-armed, the subduer of foes.

sanskrit: vānarāṃś ca raṇe bhagnān āpatantaṃ ca rāvaṇam samīkṣya rāghavo hṛṣṭo madhye jagrāha kārmukam
english: Observing the monkeys broken in battle and Rāvaṇa charging, Rāghava, exhilarated, gripped his bow in the midst of it all.

sanskrit: visphārayitum ārebhe tataḥ sa dhanur uttamam mahāvegaṃ mahānādaṃ nirbhindann iva medinīm
english: Then he began to draw that excellent bow of mighty force and great sound, as if cleaving the very earth.

sanskrit: tayoḥ śarapathaṃ prāpya rāvaṇo rājaputrayoḥ sa babhūva yathā rāhuḥ samīpe śaśisūryayoḥ
english: Coming within arrow-range of those two princes, Rāvaṇa became as Rāhu approaching the moon and sun together.

sanskrit: rāvaṇasya ca bāṇaughais tena rāmavispharitena ca śabdena rākṣasās tena petuś ca śataśas tadā
english: By Rāvaṇa's volleys of arrows and by the sound of Rāma's bowstring being drawn, the rākṣasas fell by hundreds at that time.

sanskrit: tam icchan prathamaṃ yoddhuṃ lakṣmaṇo niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ mumoca dhanur āyamya śarān agniśikhopamān
english: Wishing to fight him first, Lakṣmaṇa, drawing his bow, released sharp arrows resembling tongues of fire.

sanskrit: tān muktamātrān ākāśe lakṣmaṇena dhanuṣmatā bāṇān bāṇair mahātejā rāvaṇaḥ pratyavārayat
english: Those arrows barely released into the sky by the bow-bearing Lakṣmaṇa were intercepted by Rāvaṇa of great splendor with his own arrows.

sanskrit: ekam ekena bāṇena tribhis trīn daśabhir daśa lakṣmaṇasya praciccheda darśayan pāṇilāghavam
english: One arrow with one arrow, three with three, ten with ten — he severed Lakṣmaṇa's arrows, displaying the lightness of his hands.

sanskrit: abhyatikramya saumitriṃ rāvaṇaḥ samitiṃjayaḥ āsasāda tato rāmaṃ sthitaṃ śailam ivācalam
english: Passing beyond Saumitri, the battle-victorious Rāvaṇa then approached Rāma, who stood immovable as a mountain.

sanskrit: sa saṃkhye rāmam āsādya krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ vyasṛjac charavarṣāni rāvaṇo rāghavopari
english: Closing in on Rāma in combat, Rāvaṇa with eyes red from rage let loose showers of arrows upon Rāghava.

sanskrit: śaradhārās tato rāmo rāvaṇasya dhanuścyutāḥ dṛṣṭvaivāpatitāḥ śīghraṃ bhallāñ jagrāha satvaram
english: Seeing the streams of arrows loosed from Rāvaṇa's bow rushing upon him, Rāma swiftly seized broad-headed arrows without delay.

sanskrit: tāñ śaraughāṃs tato bhallais tīkṣṇaiś ciccheda rāghavaḥ dīpyamānān mahāvegān kruddhān āśīviṣān iva
english: Then Rāghava cut those volleys of arrows with his sharp broad-heads — those blazing, swift, angry arrows resembling venomous serpents.

sanskrit: rāghavo rāvaṇaṃ tūrṇaṃ rāvaṇo rāghavaṃ tathā anyonyaṃ vividhais tīkṣṇaiḥ śarair abhivavarṣatuḥ
english: Rāghava swiftly showered Rāvaṇa, and Rāvaṇa likewise showered Rāghava; those two rained upon each other with diverse sharp arrows.

sanskrit: ceratuś ca ciraṃ citraṃ maṇḍalaṃ savyadakṣiṇam bāṇavegān samudīkṣya samareṣv aparājitau
english: Those two unconquered ones in battle circled long in wondrous arcs, left and right, watching the speed of each other's arrows.

sanskrit: tayor bhūtāni vitreṣur yugapat saṃprayudhyatoḥ raudrayoḥ sāyakamucor yamāntakanikāśayoḥ
english: All beings were terrified by those two fighting simultaneously — both terrible, both discharging arrows, both resembling Death and the Ender of all things.

sanskrit: saṃtataṃ vividhair bāṇair babhūva gaganaṃ tadā ghanair ivātapāpāye vidyunmālāsamākulaiḥ
english: The sky became completely filled with their various arrows, as if at the end of the hot season it were crowded with storm-clouds wreathed with chains of lightning.

sanskrit: gavākṣitam ivākāśaṃ babhūva śūravṛṣṭibhiḥ mahāvegaiḥ sutīkṣṇāgrair gṛdhrapatraiḥ suvājitaiḥ
english: The sky appeared as though latticed by the showers of arrows from those heroes — swift, with very sharp tips, well-fletched with vulture feathers.

sanskrit: śarāndhakāraṃ tau bhīmaṃ cakratuḥ paramaṃ tadā gate 'staṃ tapane cāpi mahāmeghāv ivotthitau
english: Those two created a terrible, supreme darkness of arrows at that time, even as the sun had set, like two great storm-clouds rising up.

sanskrit: babhūva tumulaṃ yuddham anyonyavadhakāṅkṣiṇoḥ anāsādyam acintyaṃ ca vṛtravāsavayor iva
english: The battle between those two, each seeking the other's death, was tumultuous, unassailable, and inconceivable — like the battle between Vṛtra and Vāsava.

sanskrit: ubhau hi parameṣvāsāv ubhau śastraviśāradau ubhau cāstravidāṃ mukhyāv ubhau yuddhe viceratuḥ
english: For both were supreme archers, both expert in arms, both foremost among those versed in missiles; both ranged freely in battle.

sanskrit: ubhau hi yena vrajatas tena tena śarormayaḥ ūrmayo vāyunā viddhā jagmuḥ sāgarayor iva
english: For wherever either of those two moved, in that very direction waves of arrows sped — like waves of two oceans driven by the wind.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃsaktahastas tu rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ nārācamālāṃ rāmasya lalāṭe pratyamuñcata
english: Then Rāvaṇa, the weeper of the world, with hands engaged without pause, discharged a garland of iron arrows upon Rāma's forehead.

sanskrit: raudracāpaprayuktāṃ tāṃ nīlotpaladalaprabhām śirasā dhārayan rāmo na vyathāṃ pratyapadyata
english: Wearing upon his head those arrows launched from Rāvaṇa's fearsome bow — radiant as petals of the blue lotus — Rāma did not yield to pain.

sanskrit: atha mantrān api japan raudram astram udīrayan śarān bhūyaḥ samādāya rāmaḥ krodhasamanvitaḥ
english: Then Rāma, filled with anger, muttering mantras and invoking the terrible weapon, took up his arrows once more,

sanskrit: mumoca ca mahātejāś cāpam āyamya vīryavān tāñ śarān rākṣasendrāya cikṣepācchinnasāyakaḥ
english: and blazing with great energy, that valiant one, drawing his bow, discharged those arrows at the lord of rākṣasas — his arrows unbroken.

sanskrit: te mahāmeghasaṃkāśe kavace patitāḥ śarāḥ avadhye rākṣasendrasya na vyathāṃ janayaṃs tadā
english: Those arrows, striking the armor of the lord of rākṣasas that resembled a great dark cloud, caused him no pain at that time, for he was invulnerable.

sanskrit: punar evātha taṃ rāmo rathasthaṃ rākṣasādhipam lalāṭe paramāstreṇa sarvāstrakuśalo 'bhinat
english: Then Rāma, skilled in all weapons, struck again at that lord of rākṣasas standing in his chariot, splitting him in the forehead with a supreme missile.

sanskrit: te bhittvā bāṇarūpāṇi pañcaśīrṣā ivoragāḥ śvasanto viviśur bhūmiṃ rāvaṇapratikūlatāḥ
english: Those arrows, having pierced through their arrow-forms like five-headed serpents hissing, entered the earth, turned back by Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: nihatya rāghavasyāstraṃ rāvaṇaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ āsuraṃ sumahāghoraṃ anyad astraṃ samādade
english: Having destroyed Rāghava's weapon, Rāvaṇa, overwhelmed with rage, took up another weapon — an āsura weapon, immensely terrible.

sanskrit: siṃhavyāghramukhāṃś cānyān kaṅkakākamukhān api gṛdhraśyenamukhāṃś cāpi sṛgālavadanāṃs tathā
english: He sent forth arrows with the faces of lions and tigers, others with the faces of herons and crows, others with the faces of vultures and hawks, and still others with the faces of jackals.

sanskrit: īhāmṛgamukhāṃś cānyān vyāditāsyān bhayāvahān pañcāsyāṃl lelihānāṃś ca sasarja niśitāñ śarān
english: He also released sharp arrows with the faces of wolves — gaping-mouthed and terrifying — and five-headed arrows darting their tongues.

sanskrit: śarān kharamukhāṃś cānyān varāhamukhasaṃsthitān śvānakukkuṭavaktrāṃś ca makarāśīviṣānanān
english: Other arrows with the faces of asses, arrows with the faces of boars, arrows with the faces of dogs and cocks, arrows with the faces of crocodiles and venomous serpents —

sanskrit: etāṃś cānyāṃś ca māyābhiḥ sasarja niśitāñ śarān rāmaṃ prati mahātejāḥ kruddhaḥ sarpa iva śvasan
english: these and many other sharp arrows of illusion he, blazing with great energy, released against Rāma, hissing like an enraged serpent.

sanskrit: āsureṇa samāviṣṭaḥ so 'streṇa raghunandanaḥ sasarjāstraṃ mahotsāhaḥ pāvakaṃ pāvakopamaḥ
english: Penetrating that āsura weapon, the joy of the Raghu line, with immense energy, like fire itself, released the fire-weapon.

sanskrit: agnidīptamukhān bāṇāṃs tathā sūryamukhān api candrārdhacandravaktrāṃś ca dhūmaketumukhān api
english: Arrows with faces blazing like fire, also arrows with faces of the sun, arrows with faces of the full moon and the half-moon, and arrows with faces of comets —

sanskrit: grahanakṣatravarṇāṃś ca maholkāmukhasaṃsthitān vidyujjihvopamāṃś cānyān sasarja niśitāñ śarān
english: arrows of the color of planets and asterisms, arrows with faces of great meteors, and others resembling lightning-tongues — these sharp arrows he released.

sanskrit: te rāvaṇaśarā ghorā rāghavāstrasamāhatāḥ vilayaṃ jagmur ākāśe jagmuś caiva sahasraśaḥ
english: Those terrible arrows of Rāvaṇa, struck by Rāghava's weapon, dissolved in the sky and went away by the thousands.

sanskrit: tad astraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā hṛṣṭā nedus tataḥ sarve kapayaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
english: Seeing that weapon destroyed by Rāma of tireless deeds, all the monkeys of changeable form then roared with delight.
